items.title: Trump appears to share personal phone number of US senator in ploy to push permanent daylight savings
items.summary: US president urges Americans to call Tom Cotton to support bill to make daylight saving time permanent Donald Trump on Saturday put pressure on the US senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas to support a bill to make daylight saving time permanent, urging Americans to call what appeared to be the personal cellphone number of his fellow Republican and the chair of the Senate intelligence committee. The Sunshine Protection Act passed the House in July, but it faces roadblocks in the Senate, where some Republicans are strongly opposed to it. Proponents, including the president and his administration, argue that the change would provide more daylight during the times that Americans are most active. Detractors said permanent daylight saving time would lead to darker and potentially more hazardous winter mornings when children will be waiting for school buses and parents will be driving to work in darkness. articles.title: ‘고궁박물관 결혼’ 1호는 에스토니아 출신 유튜버
articles.snippet: “역사적으로 의미 깊은 곳에서 결혼식을 올리게 된 게 꿈만 같습니다.” 2일 서울 종로구 경복궁 앞에서 결혼식을 올린 에스토니아 출신 유튜버 마이 씨(27)는 환하게 웃으며 이렇게 소감을 밝혔다. 국립고궁박물관은 2일부터 다음 달 8일까지 매 주말과 공휴일에 하루 2회씩 박물관 앞 은행나무 쉼터에서 총 28쌍의 야외 결혼식을 지원하는 ‘고궁박물관에서 결혼해(고결)’를 진행한다. 국가유산을 활용하는 동시에 청년 세대의 혼인 비용 부담을 경감시키고자 시작된 사업이다. 마이 씨는 이 사업의 첫 사례로 이날 결혼식을 올렸다. 방탄소년단(BTS)을 계기로 한국 문화에 관심을 갖게 된 그는 지난해 전국춘향선발대회에서 외국인 최초로 미스 춘향 현(賢)에 선발됐으며 현재 한복 홍보대사로 활동 중이다. 유튜브에선 ‘김치귀신 마이’란 채널을 운영 중이다. 마이는 “경복궁은 처음 한복을 입은 곳이며 남편과 첫 데이트를 한 곳이기도 하다”며 “뜻깊은 곳에서 결혼식을 올릴 수 있어 감사하다”고 말했다.

articles.snippet: 북한이 3일 동해상으로 미상의 발사체를 쏘아 올리며 지난달 발생한 서부전선 비무장지대(DMZ) 북한군 지뢰 폭발 사건 발생 12일 만에 무력 도발을 감행했다. 이날 쏘아 올린 것이 미사일일 경우 올해 들어 16번째 미사일 도발이다.합동참모본부(합참)는 이날 오전 6시 40분쯤 공지를 통해 “북한이 동해상으로 미상 발사체를 발사했다”고 알렸다.합참은 현재 미국 등과 함께 북한이 이날 쏘아 올린 발사체의 제원과 수량, 비거리 등을 분석 중인 것으로 알려졌다.북한의 이번 도발은 지난달 21일 서부전선 군사분계선(MDL) 이남 지역에서 신규 수색로를 개척 중이던 우리 장병 3명이 북한군 지뢰 폭발로 부상당한지 12일 만의 일이다.한편 북한은 지난달 20일 단거리탄도미사일(SRBM)을 3시간 간격으로 총 두 발 발사한 바 있다.(서울=뉴스1)

articles.title: Behemoth! review - Pedro Pascal classical music drama hits all the wrong notes
articles.snippet: New York film festival: The actor stumbles through Tony Gilroy’s forgettable film marred by stylistic gimmicks Tony Gilroy has built a sturdy career as the director of the Bourne films and show runner of the popular Star Wars spin-off Andor. He directed Tilda Swinton all the way to an Oscar for her remarkable performance in the legal potboiler Michael Clayton. As the first feature film he has directed since 2012’s The Bourne Legacy, the classical music drama Behemoth! promised to be an intriguing return from a master of threading the needle between slick action and deeply felt drama. His new film comes with a score from nine A-list composers who have banded together and called themselves The Behemoth! Collective, a stacked cast and a womanizing central character who looks phenomenal in a tux: “Tár for straight men”, as a friend of mine put it. Continue reading...

articles.title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall review – Paul Thomas Anderson’s sumptuous recording is an immediate classic
articles.snippet: New York Film Festival: The Geese frontman mesmerizes in a concert film that is both swoony and austere One night last December, weary from a busy week and the impending doom of winter, I hurried into Carnegie Hall to witness Cameron Winter. The Geese frontman was marking the end of a breakout year with a series of rapturously received solo acoustic shows, drawing the penitent for whom the 23-year-old’s primordial voice struck some kind of destabilizing natural frequency. I had bought the ticket months earlier, after being hypnotized by Winter’s beguiling debut solo album, Heavy Metal, and sat transfixed in the rafters, far from the Brooklynite’s lanky, stygian presence before a single piano. So far, in fact, that I assumed the maybe-camera that came on stage at one point was a bit, perhaps a jab at our incessant need to film things from a very deadpan celebrity whose only non-music interlude that evening was to wordlessly stand, stretch and mockingly fight with the stage door, as if trying to escape his own momentous show. I emerged from the event teary, charged by what felt like a communion across time, and confused by a friend’s text: “can’t wait for the cameron winter PTA doc”. Continue reading...

articles.title: How Bassam Tariq pivoted from stalled Blade reboot to new Mahershala Ali thriller: ‘I’m happier I made this movie’
articles.snippet: In the film-maker’s Houston-set film, Ali stars as a devout Muslim who moonlights as a vicious hitman Mahershala Ali is swinging around a blade in Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother. That’s not a nod to Ali’s previous attachment to Marvel’s Blade. It’s of a piece with Ali’s character, Latif, a devout Muslim who also happens to be a contract killer, though he fashions himself a righteous killer. Latif justifies his violence as divine retribution, dispensing victims he believes to have offended God. His sword, according to writer and director Bassam Tariq, is a part of Latif’s code, a negotiation with his faith. “You are forced to strike with intention when you use a sword,” Tariq says, speaking in a recent interview in Toronto.
